```{r}
} else {
  "."
}
map_png <- file.path(qmd_dir, "email_map.png")
```

::: {.email-body}

::: {.email-preamble}

Hi all, 

A new Mouse Forecast is now available, and some changes to the way we communicate these updates.

**We have launched a new website - [mouseforecast.com](https://mouseforecast.com)** - where you can see the full report with the most up-to-date information. 

We will regularly update the website as new data comes in (and continue to send these emails at key times of the growing year). A pdf copy is also attached to this email, feel free to forward on to your relevant network along with the website URL.  

Mouse activity estimates are now completely based on quantitative data. Live-trap, active burrow, chew card assessments are integrated with citizen reports via [MouseAlert](https://feralscan.org.au/mousealert). We have kept the same "traffic light" colour coding, but shifted to a continous scale to show detail. We are actively refining statistical methods to improve estimates, and improve their presentation. Again, we welcome any feedback you may have. 

Cheers, Matt.

<div class="email-signature">
<strong>Dr Matthew Rees</strong><br>
Research Scientist | CSIRO | <a href="mailto:matt.rees@csiro.au">matt.rees@csiro.au</a>
</div>

:::

```{r}
#| label: fig-aez
#| results: asis

# Embed the PNG as a plain <img> tag with an inline base64 data URI, bypassing
# Quarto's figure wrapper (which adds a lightbox link and scroll controls).
cat(sprintf(
  '<img src="%s" style="width:100%%;height:auto;display:block;margin:12px auto 0;" alt="Mouse activity map" />',
  knitr::image_uri(map_png)
))
```
